venture.summary: Should OpenAI command an over $1 trillion valuation with this round, it would break records as the most highly valued private company ever.

venture.headline: From Toast to Bessemer: Who founders will hear from at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026
venture.summary: Hosted by TechCrunch in partnership with Fidelity Private Shares, the full-day event goes beyond fundraising and AI to explore the realities of finding customers, building teams, sharpening a pitch, developing founder leadership, and scaling companies both inside and outside traditional startup hubs.

venture.summary: The company plans to begin testing Pony.ai's robotaxis in Kazakhstan's capital in the first half of 2027.

research.headline: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
research.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores.

research.headline: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
research.summary: Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs. What happens to data after a model responds?

research.headline: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
research.summary: Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online.

research.headline: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
research.summary: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions.

research.headline: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
research.summary: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to train agents that adapt quickly to unseen tasks from limited interaction, but this requires representing task evidence over long interaction histories. Classical recurrent agents compress experience into hidden states, while transformer-based agents retrieve from past trajectories at quadratic memory and computation cost. In this work, we propose Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (METTA) for meta-reinforcement learning.

In a blog post on Friday, OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content "without risk of affecting external systems." The model, called Canva Craft, uses a two-stage architecture that allows it to plan a design before generating an image, allowing for "greater precision, consistency and control," according to an […].

regulatory.headline: Federal Court Permanently Shuts Down Illegal Debt Relief Scheme
regulatory.summary: At the FTC's request, a federal court permanently banned the operators of an alleged debt relief scheme that targeted seniors and veterans. The scheme impersonated government agencies, banks, and credit card companies. The court entered a $106.8 million judgment and ordered the defendants to turn over their assets.

regulatory.headline: FTC Reports Older Adults Lose Most Money to Investment Scams
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission submitted its annual report to Congress detailing efforts to protect older adults from fraud. According to the report, older adults lose far more money to investment scams than to any other fraud type. The document highlights key trends derived from fraud reports and outlines agency actions to address the problem.

regulatory.summary: Agency alleges corporate and individual defendants deceived travelers seeking passport services by impersonating the federal government The Federal Trade Commission is taking action against GovAssist LLC, Entry LLC and Scott Zuckerman , for their alleged involvement in a government impersonation scheme that deceived consumers.

regulatory.summary: Order addresses concerns that proposed deal would harm competition in markets for media agency services and audience data services The Federal Trade Commission has taken steps to preserve competition in the digital advertising ecosystem by requiring Publicis Groupe S.A.

regulatory.summary: FTC alleges the merger of close rivals would significantly reduce price and quality competition in already concentrated market for outdoor commercial playground equipment Today, the Federal Trade Commission sued to block Platinum Equity and its portfolio company PlayPower’s acquisition of BCI Burke, alleging the deal to combine two of the largest commercial outdoor playground equipment makers will drive up prices and decrease innovation and quality for equipment bought by schools, churches, parks and recreation departments and other organizations across the coun.

frontier.headline: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
frontier.summary: Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures.

frontier.headline: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
frontier.summary: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement. While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement.

frontier.headline: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation
frontier.summary: We develop an end-to-end framework for assessing a quantum-computing application in industrial materials science: the screening of strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials for SOFCs and SOECs. We formulate the materials problem in terms of interface observables including oxygen-vacancy formation energies, vacancy migration barriers, and electronic conductivity. We describe how these observables can be obtained using a diagrammatic GW-based embedding, either GW+DMFT or self-energy embedding theory (SEET), applied to a DFT-screened shortlist.

frontier.headline: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
frontier.summary: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix. In realistic quantum systems, however, noise is unavoidable and the projected states are generally mixed. Whether mixed-state deep thermalization admits an analogous universal limiting distribution has remained unclear.

frontier.headline: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
frontier.summary: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched Rényi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality.

industry.headline: Demi Adejuyigbe Thinks You Should Only Post 3 Times a Day
industry.summary: The comedian sees being online as similar to visiting the zoo. “I don’t need to interact with that,” he says. “It’s just a thing that I enjoy, and then I walk away.”.

voices.headline: Venezuelans face political uncertainty and infrastructure collapse following US intervention
voices.summary: Following the U.S. military operation that removed Nicolás Maduro, a new U.S.-backed arrangement with Delcy Rodríguez has left Venezuela's oil industry opaque and infrastructure severely neglected. Despite persistent economic turmoil, blackouts, and recent earthquake devastation, democratic opposition figures press for elections while citizens rely on local community efforts.

voices.headline: Trump's fiscal policies push total US debt toward forty-five trillion dollars
voices.summary: Donald Trump's tax reductions, IRS audit cuts, and military spending expanded the U.S. annual deficit to approximately two trillion dollars. Despite promises to eliminate national debt through tariffs and efficiency measures, his administration added trillions in direct costs. Consequently, total U.S. national debt is projected to reach forty-five trillion dollars by 2028.

voices.headline: Like Ken Paxton, Without the Baggage
voices.summary: A crucial midterm contest is happening right now in Texas, one that could determine the future of the state and its influence on federal policy and national politics. Senate race—though everyone is watching that one, and with good reason. The Republican, Ken Paxton—who has served as Texas’s attorney general since 2015—is an unusually weak candidate, beset by personal and financial scandals and a reputation for using his office for right-wing culture-war fixations, and weighed down by a deeply unpopular president.

voices.headline: Why So Many Men Aren’t Working
voices.summary: This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Thirty years ago this summer, the sociologist William Julius Wilson published When Work Disappears , in which he attributed high unemployment in urban, largely Black neighborhoods to structural changes in the economy. Conservatives dismissed his argument, contending instead that the problem was a poor work ethic enabled by a welfare system in desperate need of reform.

voices.headline: This Is Not a Cycle of Retribution
voices.summary: Donald Trump has spent nearly two years investigating, suing, or prosecuting anybody in politics, media, or government who ever defied him. Now, with Democrats poised to win control of one or both chambers of Congress, the administration and its allies are prepared to slip back into their familiar pose of victimhood. The putative evidence of imminent GOP persecution comes from Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, who recently told the Vox journalist Astead Herndon during an event at the University of Chicago that Democrats should pursue accountability for the administration to, among other goals, deter new graduates from enlisting in corrupt schemes.
